purpose: Quantify what the P0627 hypothesis-generating candidate actually fixes, what it does not fix, and how uncertain its apparent gains are.

selected_candidate.selection_source: one of two P0627 opened-data rule passers; selected for the lower raw RMS
selected_candidate.formula: q_selected=q_constant+0.5[max(q_potential,q_surface)-q_constant] with the frozen -67.5 degree self-coupled angular route

galaxy_evaluation.procedure: For every galaxy fold, refit the universal atomic parameters on the other four folds and predict the held-out fold; never fit an individual galaxy formula parameter.
comparators: fixed RAR with the same nuisance solution
weak-prior NFW with two per-galaxy halo parameters fitted on inner radii

regimes.surface_density: tertiles determined inside each held-out prediction table only for descriptive reporting

cross_domain_comparators.derived_cluster: NFW-derived equivalent-acceleration target; descriptive, not raw theory-neutral evidence
cross_domain_comparators.raw_scalar: original P0618 scalar at the same fixed geometry
cross_domain_comparators.compact_halo_scope: limited historical validation comparator, not a full dark-matter posterior

interpretation_rules.bootstrap: Report paired galaxy-resampling intervals; an interval above zero is repeatability within this spent sample, not external confirmation.
interpretation_rules.regime: Require both dwarf and giant absolute mean bias to fall relative to the constant control before saying the density split improved.
interpretation_rules.raw: Report every system; a small aggregate gain cannot hide a large individual worsening.
interpretation_rules.theory: Do not call the candidate a field theory without a local covariant equation, conservation law, and independent predictions.

claim_limits: The selected beta and phase came from an opened-data atlas on project-spent systems.
Five-fold galaxy OOF predictions prevent per-galaxy fitting but do not create an external sample.
Galaxy nuisance parameters were inherited from the same inner-radius RAR refit used by earlier stages.
The compact-halo comparator is limited and not matched to a full dark-matter model-selection analysis.
The candidate remains phenomenological and has more than one universal constant.
